title: Connected actions preserving a central multiplicative-type extension are trivial
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All group schemes are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A group scheme is of multiplicative type if it is isomorphic to $D(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$, with comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$ on the group-algebra basis. Let $q:E\to Q$ be a homomorphism whose coordinate-ring map is faithfully flat, meaning that extension of scalars is exact and detects zero modules, and let $N=\ker q$ be its scheme-theoretic kernel. Assume $N$ and $Q$ are of multiplicative type and $N$ is central in $E$: for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, all $n\in N(A)$ and $e\in E(A)$ commute in $E(A)$. Let $G$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] affine $F$-group scheme of finite type. Every action $a:G\times_F E\to E$ by group-scheme automorphisms that preserves $N$ is trivial: $a$ is the second projection. Here preserving $N$ means that $a$ restricts to an action on $N$, and being an action by group-scheme automorphisms means that for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $x\in G(A)$, the map $a(x,-):E(A)\to E(A)$ is a group automorphism, naturally under change of $A$.

source.place: Corollary 12.41, printed p.244, corrected by the Chapter 12 erratum at the end of this PDF: N must be central in H; faithful-flat quotient formulation.

proof.text: The map $q$ is an fpqc cover. Indeed, for every affine $T=\operatorname{Spec}B\to Q=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the affine fibre-product formula gives $E_T=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_R\mathcal O(E))$. Faithful flatness survives this base change, hence $E_T\to T$ is flat by the affine flatness criterion and surjective by the spectrum criterion. For each affine open $V\subseteq T$, the same formula makes its inverse image affine and surjective onto $V$; this is the defining fpqc covering condition. We will use these covers for products with $G$, and with further copies of $Q$ or $G$. A product of two copies of $q$, such as $G\times_FE\times_FE\to G\times_FQ\times_FQ$, is the composite $G\times_FE\times_FE\to G\times_FQ\times_FE\to G\times_FQ\times_FQ$ of two such base changes of $q$, hence an fpqc cover by stability of fpqc coverings under composition. The kernel definition also gives $E\times_F N\simeq E\times_QE$: on every algebra the maps are $(e,n)\mapsto(e,en)$ and $(e,e')\mapsto(e,e^{-1}e')$, since $q(e)=q(e')$ exactly when $e^{-1}e'\in N$.

source.place: Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), affine-cover application; flatness and faithful-flat spectrum criteria are Tags 01U5 and 00HQ; kernel-pair calculation is explicit.

proof.text: Descend $q\circ a:G\times_F E\to Q$ along $p=1_G\times q$. On its overlap write the two lifts as $e,en$ using step 1. Preservation of $N$ and the homomorphism property give $q(a(g,en))=q(a(g,e)a(g,n))=q(a(g,e))$. Representable fpqc descent therefore gives a unique $F$-morphism $b:G\times_FQ\to Q$ with $b(g,q(e))=q(a(g,e))$. It is over $F$ because the two structure maps agree after $p$. The unit law, $b(gg',t)=b(g,b(g',t))$, and $b(g,tt')=b(g,t)b(g,t')$ can each be checked after the corresponding product cover by $E$: substitution of the displayed formula reduces them to the unit, action, and homomorphism laws for $a$. Uniqueness in representable descent proves the identities before pulling back. Thus $b$ is an action by group-scheme automorphisms, with inverse at $g$ given by $g^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms); the quotient action used in Milne Corollary 12.41, p.244, with overlap and law checks written out.

proof.text: Apply connected-action rigidity to the restricted action on $N$ and to $b$ on $Q$. Both target groups are of multiplicative type, and the acting group is the given smooth connected affine finite-type $G$ over the algebraically closed field $F$. No smoothness of $N$ or $Q$ is needed. We obtain $a(g,n)=n$ and $b(g,t)=t$ on all algebra-valued points, hence $q(a(g,e))=q(e)$.

source.place: Corollary 12.37 and first sentence of the proof of corrected Corollary 12.41, printed p.244.

proof.text:
Define $c(g,e)=a(g,e)e^{-1}$. By step 3 its composite with $q$ is the identity section, so the kernel fibre product makes $c$ a morphism $G\times_F E\to N$. On the overlap, $c(g,en)=a(g,e)n(en)^{-1}=c(g,e)$ because $a(g,n)=n$. Representable descent along $p$ gives an $F$-morphism $d:G\times_FQ\to N$ with $d(g,q(e))=c(g,e)$. For any algebra and $g,e,e'$ one has
$$c(g,ee')=a(g,e)a(g,e')e'^{-1}e^{-1}=c(g,e)e\,c(g,e')e^{-1}=c(g,e)c(g,e'),$$
since $c(g,e')\in N$ and $N$ is central in $E$. Also $c(g,1)=1$. Pull back the proposed homomorphism identity for $d$ along the fpqc cover $G\times_F E\times_F E\to G\times_FQ\times_FQ$ and use this calculation; uniqueness in descent proves it downstairs. Thus $d$ is a family of homomorphisms $Q\to N$. Finally $d(1_G,-)=1$: this holds after the cover $q$, since $a(1_G,e)=e$, and descends by uniqueness.

source.place: Corrected Corollary 12.41, printed p.244: the two factorizations apply to the difference a(g,e)e^{-1}, not to a itself. Centrality is used in the displayed multiplicativity calculation; descent is Stacks Tag 023Q.

proof.text: Use homomorphism-family rigidity with $X=G$, $x_0=1_G$, $D_1=Q$, $D_2=N$, and $\phi=d$. Its hypotheses hold by the item and step 4: $G$ is affine, connected and of finite type, $N,Q$ are diagonalizable over $F$, and the family consists of homomorphisms on every algebra. It gives $d(g,t)=d(1_G,t)=1$. Consequently $a(g,e)e^{-1}=c(g,e)=d(g,q(e))=1$, so $a(g,e)=e$ on every algebra. This is equality of morphisms: for the affine source $G\times_FE$, take its own coordinate algebra and its universal point to identify the comorphisms. Hence $a=\operatorname{pr}_E$.
